data.content_ref: inline:The target proposes a single unified forbidden-case rubric spanning both refusals. But the problem asks for explicit FORBIDDEN cases (plural) for the two untested refusals — specifically a typed lease-mismatch code before any provider call, and a seat-binding whose endpoint identity disagrees must not be counted as coverage. A mutation that homogenizes identity comparisons across BOTH logic paths does not name a concrete mutation that would today pass the suite silently for either individual refusal: for refusal (1) the silent-pass risk is a comparator that skips the lease-mismatch code or proceeds to a provider call despite drift, and for refusal (2) it is a comparator that counts mismatched seat/endpoint identity as coverage. Bundling them into one rubric does not provide a machine-checkable forbidden case for each refusal; it leaves each refusal's specific mutation unnamed, and the countercondition concedes structural failure if separate cases are demanded.
